title: Microsoft 365 Copilot: admins deploy and govern MCP-based agents in the Microsoft 365 admin center
summary: Hold: Microsoft documents preview automation for the publisher-category and User access settings, contrary to the page's claim that these are portal-only controls. The roadmap facts and MCP server procedures are supported; two paths stop before the deciding control, and the checklist names consent and monitoring controls missing from the table.

claims.where: controls[3].ui; Governance controls; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Agents > Settings > Agent and plugin access is the Microsoft 365 admin center path to publisher-category access settings.
claims.quote: Select Agents > Settings > Agent and plugin access. ... Under the installation settings, choose which publisher categories users can access.

claims.where: controls[3].api; Governance controls: no API for any control
claims.claim: Microsoft documents no API or automation for Agent and plugin access, so it is a portal-only action.
claims.quote: These resources also support remediation and applyOnce. ... allowedagenttypes resource type ... Controls which types of apps, agents, and plugins users can see in their store and install.
claims.fix: Set controls[3].api to kind 'graph', call 'POST /beta/admin/configurationManagement/configurationMonitors', docs 'https://learn.microsoft.com/graph/api/configurationmanagement-post-configurationmonitors?view=graph-rest-beta'. Append to its note: 'Preview TCM automation uses mode=applyOnce and baseline.resources with resourceType=microsoft.agent.allowedagenttypes, resourceVersion=1, and properties.valueObject fields areMicrosoftAppsAllowed, areTenantScopedAppsAllowed, areISVAppsAllowed and areMicrosoftCertifiedThirdPartyAppsAllowed. It requires the signed-in AI Administrator and delegated permissions described at https://learn.microsoft.com/graph/utcm-agent-resources; TCM applyOnce is global-service only.' Cite that resource page and https://learn.microsoft.com/graph/utcm-remediation-applyonce-resources. Replace the blanket portal-only sentence with 'Microsoft documents preview TCM automation for Agent and plugin access and User access; no matching automation was found for the three MCP server controls at the time of writing (November 2026).'

claims.fix: Append to controls[3].note: 'The Agent settings page instead labels the third category Allow agents and plugins built by external publishers.' Keep the cited MCP management page's wording attributed to that page; both pages are already in sources.

claims.claim: Microsoft documents no API or automation for User access, so it is a portal-only action.
claims.quote: useraccess resource type ... userAssignmentCategory ... Specifies whether all users or no users can access agents and plugins. ... everyone, noOne
claims.fix: Set controls[4].api to kind 'graph', call 'POST /beta/admin/configurationManagement/configurationMonitors', docs 'https://learn.microsoft.com/graph/api/configurationmanagement-post-configurationmonitors?view=graph-rest-beta'. Append to its note: 'Preview TCM automation uses mode=applyOnce and baseline.resources with resourceType=microsoft.agent.useraccess, resourceVersion=1, and properties.valueObject.userAssignmentCategory set to everyone or noOne. This reference does not document selecting specific users or groups through this resource. It requires the signed-in AI Administrator and delegated permissions described at https://learn.microsoft.com/graph/utcm-agent-resources; TCM applyOnce is global-service only.' Cite that resource page and https://learn.microsoft.com/graph/utcm-remediation-applyonce-resources. Apply the replacement of the blanket portal-only sentence specified for Agent and plugin access.
